Title: Asking LLM for confidence
Description: LLM-based agents can do a lot of tasks. Or, at least, they can appear to do them. For example, they write code, summarize papers, plan trips, and fill in forms. If you ask one for a probability or a confidence score, it will give you one of those too. I have seen many agent designers use LLMs to generate confidence scores in this way. The problem is that there is no good reason to trust that number. This post is about why we cannot rely on an LLM to generate a confidence score.

Title: The Rise of Highly Personal Software – Michael Bassili
Description: I think there’s a strong desire for uniquely personalized software permeating the market these days, spurred by the commodification of cheap large language models from Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google. We saw companies try their hand as enabling this kind of behaviour through MCP and other model-level integrations, but Muse and other forms of agentic helper tools have turned the tides again. My friend is using Muse to help him look for a new apartment. Unlike the APIs of yesteryear, foundation models are really good at distilling vague, nebulous requirements into tangible outcomes.
